title: Modular Inverse Calculator
description: Compute a⁻¹ mod m with the extended Euclidean algorithm — and learn why no inverse exists when gcd ≠ 1.
howto: Enter a and the modulus m.
Follow the Euclid steps to the inverse, or see why none exists.

faqs.q: When does a modular inverse exist?
faqs.a: Exactly when gcd(a, m) = 1, i.e. a and m are coprime. Otherwise no x can satisfy a·x ≡ 1 (mod m).

faqs.q: What is the extended Euclidean algorithm?
faqs.a: It tracks the Bézout coefficients while running Euclid’s algorithm, producing x with a·x + m·y = gcd.
RSA key generation, modular division in cryptography, and solving linear congruences.
